title: 1 man, 2 children dead in Burlington, Ont., house fire, Ontario Fire Marshal says
summary: A man, a 12-year-old child and a one-year-old boy are dead following a house fire in Burlington, Ont., the Ontario Fire Marshal said Monday morning in a news briefing.

image.caption: Jon Pegg, the province's fire marshal, announced the deaths of three people in a Burlington, Ont., house fire at the Burlington Fire Department Nov. 16. (Justin Chandler/CBC)

blocks.text: Hamilton
A man, a 12-year-old child and a one-year-old boy are dead following a house fire in Burlington, Ont., the Ontario Fire Marshal said Monday morning in a news briefing.
A woman and another child remain in critical condition, the Fire Marshal said
· CBC News
· Posted: Nov 16, 2026 11:36 AM EST | Last Updated: 1 hour ago
A man, a 12-year-old child and a one-year-old boy are dead after a house fire in Burlington, Ont., the Ontario Fire Marshal said Monday morning in a news briefing.
A woman and another child, who police said over the weekend is under five years old, are in critical condition, said Fire Marshal Jon Pegg who added that they were all members of the same family.
Pegg offered his "sincere condolences to the family, friends, neighbours and all of the community on the tragic event."
Emergency crews were called to a townhouse complex near Maple Crossing Boulevard and Freeman Street at around 6:50 a.m. on Saturday, Burlington Fire Department said in a news release.

items: 3 kids, 2 adults in life-threatening condition after Burlington house fire: Halton police

blocks.text: The department said it sent 31 people and nine vehicles to respond. Firefighters rescued two adults and three children, taking them to hospital in life-threatening condition, Halton police Const. Ryan Anderson told CBC News at the scene Saturday.
Burlington Mayor Marianne Meed Ward attended the news conference Monday, telling reporters after that the fire was "absolutely devastating."
A man and two children are dead following a fire at a Burlington home, the Ontario Fire Marshal said on Monday. (Spencer Gallichan-Lowe/CBC)
Also on Monday, Pegg thanked first-responders, including firefighters, who were "nothing short of incredible and heroic."
"They rushed into what could only be described as an inferno trying to rescue those family members and literally risk their own lives doing so," he said.
Pegg said the investigation is ongoing and findings will be released once it's done.
Initially, three patients were reported as vital signs absent, Burlington Fire Chief Drew Boys said Saturday.
Burlington house fire leaves 3 children, 2 adults in critical condition
The local fire department contacted the Ontario Fire Marshal because the fire required people to be sent to hospital.
The fire started in the bedroom and smoke and flames were showing, Burlington Fire said. It estimated the costs of the damage at $350,000.
On Saturday, neighbour Sasha Guerriero said she woke up in the morning to the smell of smoke and the sounds of smashing glass and people yelling.
"It's probably one of the most traumatizing things I've ever seen. It's awful," she said, adding she doesn't know the family, but has played with the kids when they run around outside.
"The kids are lovely. Really good, nice kids."
Burlington Fire Chief Drew Boys said smoke and flames were visible from the house when firefighters arrived Saturday morning. (Justin Chandler/CBC)
Fire marshal says preventative measures save lives
During Monday's fire briefing, Pegg said he wanted to focus on "safety messaging," as the colder months see "the highest increase in fatalities."
"I sound like a broken record but working smoke alarms truly do save lives," he said.
Fire Marshal spokesperson Jim Demetriou said Monday it was still under investigation whether the house in Burlington had working alarms.
Pegg said people should test smoke alarms every month and set up an escape plan.

"You can't have one without the other so when that alarm goes off you need to know in advance what I'm going to do with my family to get out safely. It's the only thing that will save your family's life," he said.
Pegg said people should have two ways out of every room.
"Practice it often, talk about it with your kids if you have kids. If you have people who need extra assistance at the time of an emergency, plan for that in advance," he said.
